content.text: 26	Our central finding is that architectural variation produces structured predictive multiplicity whose magnitude depends on task type, not attention ratio. The ambiguity $\alpha$ \citep{marx2020predictive} ranges from 0.14 (PIQA) to 0.30 (LAMBADA), varies $2\times$ across task types but only 0.03 within each benchmark across attention ratios; pairwise Jaccard remains uniformly low ($\leq 0.10$, all $p < .01$ across all ten five-architecture pairs). A second finding is that per-example overlap appears to stabilize at the first attention level (4\%) and remains flat at higher ratios. Even on LAMBADA, where aggregate variance shows a non-significant decreasing trend ($\rho = -1.0$, Bonferroni-adjusted $p = .170$; at 1.3B only), per-example Jaccard does not change (\S\ref{ssec:decoupling}).

5	We have shown that hybrid linear recurrent architectures which appear interchangeable by aggregate benchmarks diverge substantially at the per-example level. This multiplicity varies by task type ($\alpha = 0.14$--$0.30$) rather than attention ratio. Per-example overlap appears to stabilize at 4\% attention (pairwise Jaccard $\leq 0.10$); two interpretations (architecture-specific fingerprints or rapid convergence toward Transformer-like behavior) remain open (Appendix~\ref{app:transformer_entrainment}). Confidence margins partially predict affected examples (AUC 0.70--0.74), with rescue thresholds architecture-invariant but disruption thresholds varying 47\%.
